answers.question: What does my plan have me doing this week, and why?
answers.text:
Here’s what your plan has you doing this week, from Monday, August 31 to Sunday, September 6:

- Monday, August 31: Walk 20 minutes at a comfortable pace (a training day)
- Tuesday, September 1: Rest day (a rest day)
- Wednesday, September 2: Run/walk intervals: walk 5 minutes to warm up, then alternate easy jogging with walking breaks. 15 minutes of easy jogging (a training day)
- Thursday, September 3: Rest day (a rest day)
- Friday, September 4: Rest day (a rest day)
- Saturday, September 5: Run/walk intervals: 15 minutes of easy jogging broken into short efforts, with walking breaks after each effort (a training day)
- Sunday, September 6: Rest day (a rest day)

In total, the plan schedules 30 minutes of jogging this week.

Why? You’re in the Base phase of your long-term plan, which runs from Monday, August 31 to Sunday, September 13. This is week 1 of the plan. Your average jogging minutes per week over the recent weeks before this plan was 0 min, so the plan starts gently to build a foundation.

answers.question: What does my plan look like over the next few months?
answers.text:
Your long-term plan runs from Monday, August 31 to Sunday, November 22, covering 12 weeks across 6 phases. You are currently in week 1 of the Base phase, which lasts until Sunday, September 13. The next phase begins on Monday, September 14.

Here is the phase breakdown:

Base: Monday, August 31 to Sunday, September 13 (2 weeks). Build the foundation for your weight-loss plan by making movement feel normal again without overdoing it.
Build: Monday, September 14 to Sunday, October 11 (4 weeks). Increase the challenge gently as your body adapts to walking and easy jogging.
Recovery: Monday, October 12 to Sunday, October 18 (1 week). Let your body absorb the work with easy walking that protects your momentum and your joints.
Base: Monday, October 19 to Sunday, October 25 (1 week). Reestablish a steady routine after the recovery week without rushing back into hard sessions.
Build: Monday, October 26 to Sunday, November 8 (2 weeks). Rebuild the week's workload gradually while keeping the scale moving in the right direction.
Maintain: Monday, November 9 to Sunday, November 22 (2 weeks). Protect the routine you have built and make it feel like a normal part of your week.

And the weekly sessions:

Week 1, starting Monday, August 31 (Base): key session Run/walk (run). Build the foundation for your weight-loss plan by making movement feel normal again without overdoing it.
Week 2, starting Monday, September 7 (Base): key session Easy (walk). Strengthen the habit of getting out the door so consistency starts to support your fat-loss progress.
Week 3, starting Monday, September 14 (Build): key session Easy (run). Increase the challenge gently as your body adapts to walking and easy jogging.
Week 4, starting Monday, September 21 (Build): key session Intervals (run). Keep the effort comfortable while making the active week a bigger contributor to your calorie balance.
Week 5, starting Monday, September 28 (Build): key session Run/walk (run). Add variety to the run-walk mix so the routine stays interesting and your progress continues.
Week 6, starting Monday, October 5 (Build): key session Intervals (run). Ask for a little more from your legs while keeping the work controlled and sustainable.
Week 7, starting Monday, October 12 (Recovery): key session Recovery (walk). Let your body absorb the work with easy walking that protects your momentum and your joints.
Week 8, starting Monday, October 19 (Base): key session Easy (run). Reestablish a steady routine after the recovery week without rushing back into hard sessions.
Week 9, starting Monday, October 26 (Build): key session Run/walk (run). Rebuild the week's workload gradually while keeping the scale moving in the right direction.
Week 10, starting Monday, November 2 (Build): key session Intervals (run). Keep your sessions consistent and your effort honest as the plan continues toward your weight goal.
Week 11, starting Monday, November 9 (Maintain): key session Easy (walk). Protect the routine you have built and make it feel like a normal part of your week.
Week 12, starting Monday, November 16 (Maintain): key session Easy (run). Close the plan with a sustainable mix of walking and jogging that you can carry forward.

Your recent jogging baseline is 0 minutes per week.

answers.text: Your weight has increased since you stopped running regularly. From Thu Mar 5 to Sat May 23, your average body mass was 168.8 lb. In the period after your last run on Sat May 23, from Sun May 24 to Sun Aug 30, your average body mass rose to 173.6 lb, reaching a maximum of 179.2 lb. Your body fat percentage also increased, from 16.3% to 17.3%. Interestingly, your lean body mass also went up, from 141.3 lb to 143.4 lb. That suggests the weight gain included both fat and lean tissue. Since that last run, you have recorded only walking workouts.
